claims.assessment: abundant achievements as general and minister

skill.en: Khitan and Chinese script; astronomy and physiognomy

translationRepairs: Yelu Longyun was born Han Dezang, son of Kuangsi, the Southwestern Frontier Pacification Commissioner.
Yelu Longyun was born Han Derang, son of Kuangsi, the Southwestern Frontier Pacification Commissioner.
名德讓 gives the personal name Derang (讓 ràng), not Dezang; the idiomatic mistranscription is a real naming error and Han Derang restores it.
Yelu Longyun, originally surnamed Han, named Dezang, was the son of the Southwestern Frontier Pacification Commissioner Kuangsi.
Yelu Longyun, originally surnamed Han, named Derang, was the son of the Southwestern Frontier Pacification Commissioner Kuangsi.
名德讓 is Derang; the literal named Dezang misreads 讓 and the proposed Derang matches the Chinese.
He fell out with Han Dezang over a matter of policy. Dezang, enraged, seized a guard's weapon and struck him on the head, killing him outright.
He fell out with Han Derang over a matter of policy. Derang, enraged, seized a guard's weapon and struck him on the head, killing him outright.
與韓德讓…德讓怒 names Han Derang twice; replacing Dezang with Derang corrects the same 讓/ràng misreading without changing the clash or killing.
Appraisal: During Tonghe, Dezang held the powers of both general and minister. In defeating enemies, advancing worthy men, and sustaining the state, his achievements were abundant indeed.
Appraisal: During Tonghe, Derang held the powers of both general and minister. In defeating enemies, advancing worthy men, and sustaining the state, his achievements were abundant indeed.
論曰：德讓在統和間 begins the appraisal with Derang; Dezang is the same false reading of 讓 and Derang is the accurate replacement.
As the empress's uterine younger brother, his favor at court grew day by day.
As the empress's younger brother, his favor at court grew day by day.
以皇后外弟 marks him as the empress's younger brother (natal/affine 外弟); uterine (同母) is not in the Chinese, so dropping that invented qualifier is correct.
At the end of Qianheng, when his father's mourning period ended he was forcibly recalled to office and served provisionally as Southwestern Pacification Commissioner.
At the end of Qianheng, when he was in mourning for his father he was forcibly recalled to office and served provisionally as Southwestern Pacification Commissioner.
丁父喪 means he was in mourning for his father; 強起復職 is forced recall from mourning. The literal's 'mourning period ended' reverses the Chinese, and the proposed wording matches it.
When Emperor Jingzong fell gravely ill, he and Yelu Xiezhen together received the dying command: they enthroned the Prince of Liang, made the empress dowager, and she assumed regency.

When Emperor Jingzong fell gravely ill, he and Yelu Xiezhen together received the dying command: they enthroned the Prince of Liang as emperor, made the empress the empress dowager, and she assumed regency.

立梁王為帝，皇后為皇太后 requires both elevating the Prince of Liang as emperor and turning the empress into empress dowager. The original omits that transition; the proposal's 'made the empress empress dowager' is right in sense but awkward, so the article is restored.
